channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Updates Rules for Monopoly Control and Company Mergers
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has revised its regulations for antitrust control, including rules for company mergers, joint ventures, and state aid to businesses. The Antimonopoly Service will now review company actions that could affect market competition, such as mergers and acquisitions. New provisions also empower the service to assess the competitive impact of state financial assistance to enterprises.

item.title: New Mayor Appointed in Kara-Balta Amid Environmental Scandal
item.description: Asylbek Jenishbek has been appointed the new mayor of Kara-Balta, a city facing ongoing complaints about industrial air pollution. The appointment by President Sadyr Japarov comes amid heightened environmental concerns, with residents reporting smog and industrial emissions. Authorities have taken measures against polluting enterprises, including "Asia Steel," which was identified as a major source of emissions.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Adopt New Civil Code by End of 2027
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev emphasized justice and the rule of law in his address, outlining plans for a new Civil Code. The current code, adopted in the 1990s, has fulfilled its historical role. A new code is needed to adapt to current conditions and establish a legal basis for a future-oriented economy, providing stability for citizens, entrepreneurs, and investors. The draft is expected to be completed and adopted by the end of 2027.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Allocate 6.5 Trillion Tenge for Infrastructure Modernization
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to allocate approximately 6.5 trillion tenge from the National Fund by the end of 2029 for infrastructure modernization under the "People's Construction" program. Funds will be directed towards building and renovating schools, hospitals, roads, engineering networks, industrial, and energy facilities. The initiative aims to create hundreds of thousands of jobs, emphasizing quality of employment with fair wages, safe working conditions, and social guarantees.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to Enhance Sales Control with Fiscal Software Mandate
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has approved regulations for fiscal software with data transmission capabilities, signed by Cabinet of Ministers Chairman Adylbek Kasymaliev. This aims to improve tax administration and ensure accurate revenue accounting. Certain business activities will require mandatory use of this software, with others able to use it voluntarily.

item.title: Kazakhstan Needs Long-Term Financing System for Agriculture Development
item.description: Kazakhstan's President highlighted the need for long-term financing in agriculture, noting current short-term mechanisms like 'Keng dala' do not support large projects. The goal is to enable farmers to plan and develop production confidently. The 'Baiterek' holding is tasked with implementing promising food industry projects.

item.title: Kazakhstan Boosts Meat and Metal Exports to Tajikistan Amidst Trade Growth
item.description: Kazakhstan has significantly increased its exports of meat and metal to Tajikistan. Total trade between the two nations reached $1.1 billion in January-September 2026, a 29.5% rise. Key exports include wheat, barley, sunflower oil, beef, and steel bars, while smartphone imports from Tajikistan decreased.

item.title: Kazakhstan Considers Raising Toll Road Fees for Commercial Trucks
item.description: Kazakhstan's government is exploring ways to shift road maintenance costs onto commercial trucks, including foreign ones. A working group, chaired by Deputy Prime Minister Serik Zhumangarin, discussed proposals to make toll roads financially self-sustaining. No decisions on personal vehicle fees were made.

item.title: Zhambyl Governor Criticizes Police for Ineffective Juvenile Crime Prevention
item.description: Yerbol Karashukeyev, head of the Zhambyl region, criticized local authorities and police for formalistic approaches to preventing juvenile delinquency. He stated that current measures are not saving children's lives and that indifference is unacceptable. The governor also initiated a police performance review.

item.title: Construction Prices in Kazakhstan Outpace Inflation Over Past Year
item.description: Construction costs in Kazakhstan have risen faster than inflation, with the construction price index increasing by 10.1% year-on-year as of October 2026. While annual inflation slowed to 9.2%, construction-related work and associated costs saw significant price hikes, particularly cement and other materials.

item.title: Kazakhstan Presents Alatau City Investment Potential in Berlin
item.description: Kazakhstan's Deputy Prime Minister Kanat Bozumbayev held talks in Berlin to attract investment and technology in industry, energy, construction, and urban infrastructure for Alatau City. Discussions included establishing an investment-financial platform between Kazakhstan and Germany, a proposal previously made by President Tokayev.

item.title: Kazakhstan Strengthens Energy Independence Amid Growing Demand
item.description: Kazakhstan is enhancing its energy independence by constructing new power plants and modernizing existing infrastructure to meet rising electricity demand. Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov chaired a meeting focusing on projects by the Samruk-Kazyna fund to bolster the nation's energy sector. The goal is to achieve surplus power generation by 2029.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's virtual asset market volume reaches 2.2 trillion soms in H1 2026
item.description: The volume of operations in Kyrgyzstan's regulated virtual asset market reached 2.2 trillion soms in the first half of 2026, involving approximately 3.8 million transactions. Tax revenues from virtual asset service providers in 2025 amounted to about 1.48 billion soms. As of October 2026, 172 licensed providers operate in the country.

item.title: Two tigers released into Kazakhstan's wild after 80-year absence
item.description: Two tigers, Amur (male) and Umіt (female), have been released into the Ile-Balkhash State Nature Reserve in Kazakhstan, marking their return after an 80-year absence. The female tiger, brought from Russia, has already successfully hunted wild boar and wolves. Local residents express concerns about potential livestock predation.

item.title: Paraguayan President Resigns Amidst Bank Collapse and Protests
item.description: Paraguayan President Santiago Peña has resigned following the collapse of Ueno Bank, which left millions of customers unable to access their funds. The resignation came during a parliamentary session where lawmakers were voting on his impeachment, accusing him of conflict of interest and misuse of pension funds. The bank's failure has sparked protests across the country.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Increase Outsourcing in State Healthcare to 30% by 2030
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to expand private sector involvement in its healthcare system, aiming to procure 30% of medical services through outsourcing by 2030. The initiative, outlined in a presidential decree, also involves attracting foreign professional management companies to at least five major medical institutions to implement advanced management practices. Mechanisms for private sector engagement, considering regional healthcare needs and existing capacities, will be introduced from January 1, 2027.

item.title: Ukraine's President Zelensky Considers Online Voting for Future Elections
item.description: President Volodymyr Zelensky of Ukraine has suggested that online voting could be a viable option for future elections. He noted that the parliament would need to find a suitable solution to implement such a system. A key challenge is enabling soldiers on the front lines to vote, as current conditions make it technically impossible.

item.title: Trump Announces Potential "Massive Deal" Regarding Ukraine and Europe
item.description: Former US President Donald Trump stated that a resolution to the Russia-Ukraine war is near and that a future agreement could involve all of Europe. He described it as a "massive deal" that would make "everyone happy." Trump did not provide specific terms or a timeline for the agreement, but mentioned meeting with Russian envoy Kirill Dmitriev.

item.title: Uzbekistan Achieves Record Cotton Harvest of Over Five Million Tons
item.description: Uzbekistan has harvested over five million tons of raw cotton in 2026, a record since its independence in 1991. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev attributed this success to increased yields and mechanization, despite reduced planting areas. Farmers are expected to profit significantly.

item.title: Uzbekistan Focuses on Energy Efficiency as Investment in Sustainable Future
item.description: Uzbekistan is prioritizing energy efficiency for the autumn-winter period, focusing on heat conservation and rational resource use. Uzpsb Bank reported its "green" credit portfolio exceeded $730 million by October 1, 2026, representing 15% of its total portfolio. These funds support solar energy, energy-efficient construction materials, and infrastructure development.

item.title: Illegal Call Center Discovered in Tashkent, 23 Foreign Nationals Found
item.description: An illegal call center operating from a private residence in Tashkent's Yakkasaroy district has been uncovered by the Ministry of Internal Affairs. During a raid, 23 foreign nationals residing in Uzbekistan without proper permits were found. Authorities also seized electronic devices and passports.

item.title: Uzbek President Arrives in Astana for Central Asia Security Summit
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev of Uzbekistan has arrived in Astana, Kazakhstan, at the invitation of President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev and King Abdullah II of Jordan. He will attend a summit of Central Asian leaders focused on artificial intelligence security and countering its misuse for terrorism.

item.title: Uzbekistan Explores International Experience to Enhance Social Initiatives
item.description: Uzbekistan is focusing on improving the effectiveness of social projects and adopting international best practices. The country has established legal and organizational frameworks to support NGOs, social orders, and grants, with a current emphasis on increasing practical results and public oversight.

item.title: Kazakh Companies Sign Deals Worth $100 Million at China International Import Expo
item.description: Kazakh companies have signed agreements totaling approximately $100 million at the 9th China International Import Expo (CIIE) in Shanghai. Kazakhstan's Minister of Trade and Integration, Arman Shakkaliyev, participated in the event, which aims to expand export opportunities and attract investment. The expo is a major platform for international trade.

item.title: Yandex Lavka plans to launch robot deliveries in Tashkent by end of 2026
item.description: Yandex Uzbekistan plans to introduce autonomous robot deliveries for products, ready-made meals, and daily necessities through Yandex Lavka in Tashkent by the end of 2026. The company is currently testing the robots and preparing them for urban operation. Robots will navigate independently, using lidar and ultrasonic sensors, and can handle curbs up to 10 cm high, operating even in rain.

item.title: Uzbekistan reforms 'Women's Notebook' fund for enhanced support mechanisms
item.description: Uzbekistan has updated the 'Women's Notebook' fund mechanisms to provide new forms of assistance to women in need. Reforms include improved medical services, with up to 22 million soms for non-surgical treatment and 4.4 million soms for diagnostic tests. Housing repair assistance remains at 22 million soms, and rental subsidies have increased for women in various regions.

item.title: Regional Identity as Central Asia's Strategic Asset Amidst Global Shifts
item.description: The Think Road Forum 2026 in Tashkent focuses on 'Global Transformation and Regional Dynamics: Central Asia in the Emerging World Order.' Experts discussed regional security, economic cooperation, connectivity, and relations with global powers, emphasizing regional identity as a strategic resource for stability and development in a turbulent world.

item.title: Armenia begins design work on US-backed trade corridor despite pending agreement
item.description: Armenian officials have started design work for the TRIPP trade corridor, a project announced with the United States in January. While a preliminary agreement outlined ownership, operational details are still pending. Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan stated that preparatory work will commence immediately, even before the official incorporation of TRIPP Development.

item.title: Rosatom proposes nuclear power plant to Turkmenistan at Ashgabat conference
item.description: State Atomic Energy Corporation Rosatom presented its technological capabilities for Turkmenistan's energy sector at an international conference in Ashgabat. A model of an integrated nuclear power plant with reactors of various capacities was a central exhibit. Rosatom discussed nuclear energy, renewable energy, nuclear medicine, and logistics with Turkmen officials.

item.title: Turkmenistan's Parliament Approves New Laws and Amendments in First Ten Months
item.description: Turkmenistan's Parliament passed eight laws and 15 resolutions during the first ten months of the year. Amendments were made to laws concerning industrial safety, accounting, road infrastructure, environmental protection, water resources, and migration policy. The Parliament also accepted credentials from eight foreign ambassadors and held 48 meetings with international representatives.

item.title: Turkmenistan President Arrives in Astana for Regional Security Summit
item.description: Turkmenistan President Serdar Berdymukhamedov has arrived in Astana to attend a summit on regional security. The meeting, part of the Aqaba Process initiated in 2015, focuses on joint efforts against terrorism and extremism. The summit is scheduled for November 6th.

item.title: Turkmen President Serdar Berdimuhamedow visits Kazakhstan for AI security summit
item.description: Turkmen President Serdar Berdimuhamedow traveled to Kazakhstan to attend the high-level meeting of Central Asian leaders on artificial intelligence security within the framework of the Aqaba Process. The visit highlights the strong strategic dialogue between Turkmenistan and Kazakhstan, focusing on trade, economy, and transport corridors.

item.title: Uzbekistan Proposes Expanding Crime Prevention Bodies to Include Key Ministries
item.description: Uzbekistan is considering expanding its crime prevention system by adding entities like the Ministry of Emergency Situations, Ministry of Digital Technologies, and the Central Bank. A draft law proposes increasing prevention subjects from 14 to 21, with defined rights and obligations based on legislation.

item.title: Regional forum of trade union leaders from Central Asia and Azerbaijan held in Ashgabat
item.description: A regional forum for trade union leaders from Central Asia and Azerbaijan, organized by the National Center of Trade Unions of Turkmenistan and the International Labour Organization, took place in Ashgabat. The forum focused on improving labor relations and ensuring decent work and social justice, aligning with ILO principles.

item.title: Uzbekistan Implements New Order and Strict Control Over Drug Prices
item.description: Uzbekistan has introduced a new mechanism for regulating and controlling drug prices, effective April 1, 2025. A presidential decree aims to prevent unjustified price increases, reduce public spending on medicines, and foster a transparent market. A reference pricing system will set maximum wholesale and retail markups.

item.title: Melania Trump Delivers Letters for Putin and Zelensky at White House Meeting
item.description: First Lady Melania Trump met with Russian and Ukrainian representatives at the White House to discuss humanitarian efforts in Oleshky, Ukraine. She conveyed letters to Vladimir Putin and Volodymyr Zelensky, urging continued dialogue for civilian aid. The meeting focused on humanitarian operations.

item.title: Calls for Stronger Joint Action Against Terrorism Discussed on Tahawol Program
item.description: The Tahawol program featured discussions on the need for enhanced joint efforts to combat terrorism. The segment also briefly touched upon unrelated sports news concerning Afghanistan's cricket and futsal teams, as well as a report on a Turkish Daesh suspect's arrival in Pakistan and Trump's comments on the Afghanistan war.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Plans to Fund Private Veterinarians from State Budget
item.description: Starting January 1, 2027, Kyrgyzstan intends to pay salaries to private veterinarians from the state budget. This initiative, driven by a presidential directive, aims to improve veterinary service quality and stabilize the epidemiological situation. It also seeks to ensure the effective completion of state tasks, including animal identification.

item.title: US and Turkmenistan Deepen Economic and Diplomatic Ties with Envoy Visit
item.description: The United States and Turkmenistan are strengthening their economic and diplomatic relationship, marked by a visit from a top U.S. diplomat and a business delegation to Ashgabat. Discussions focused on expanding business ties, identifying new partnership opportunities, and U.S. support for the TAPI gas pipeline.

item.title: OSCE to Assess Feasibility of Sending Observers to Kyrgyzstan Presidential Election
item.description: The OSCE's Office for Democratic Institutions and Human Rights (ODIHR) is evaluating the possibility of sending an international observation mission to Kyrgyzstan's upcoming presidential election. The Central Election Commission met with ODIHR advisors to discuss preparations, including equipment testing, voter identification, and accessibility for people with disabilities.
